audits.title: 304 Increasing the intensity of physiotherapy in a subacute stroke rehabilitation unit—results of audit and intervention
audits.standard: National Clinical Guideline for Stroke (2023): high-intensity therapy, total of 3 hours daily, and improved reporting of exercise prescription
audits.setting: Subacute stroke rehabilitation unit, Royal Hospital Donnybrook, Dublin
audits.intervention: Stroke exercise class restructured into a twice-weekly circuit class (5 x 6-minute stations) with outdoor mobility, tally counters, more semi-supervised practice and a 'champions board'.

cycle2.result: Average recorded repetitions per week 1,043 (range 245–2095); average 462 repetitions in the exercise class.

audits.other_findings: Recording of repetitions improved each year; results may have been affected by staffing and COVID-19 restrictions.
audits.citation: McClean A. 304 Increasing the intensity of physiotherapy in a subacute stroke rehabilitation unit—results of audit and intervention. Age and Ageing. 2023;52(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afad156.239.

audits.title: Assessing Adherence to Acute Stroke Therapy Guidelines: An Audit Study
audits.standard: 2023 National Clinical Guidelines for Stroke (UK and Ireland): at least 3 hours of rehabilitation a day on at least 5 of 7 days
audits.setting: Acute stroke unit, Galway University Hospital

cycle1.result: None of 9 patients met the guideline; therapy 44 to 132 minutes a day; average 49.1% of recommended therapy; therapy assistants provided 59.3% of therapy.

audits.intervention: Two new stroke therapy assistant posts funded before the audit
audits.other_findings: Stroke assistants increased therapy time but the guideline was still not achieved.
audits.citation: Scanlan M, Harte E, Newell E. Assessing Adherence to Acute Stroke Therapy Guidelines: An Audit Study. Age and Ageing. 2024;53(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/ageing/afae178.067.

audits.title: Use of audit, feedback and education increased guideline implementation in a multidisciplinary stroke unit.
audits.standard: Australian stroke rehabilitation guideline recommendations; minimum target of 10% change per practice area

cycle1.result: Baseline audit of 27 target practice areas (baseline figures not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: Repeated audit feedback, education and training for staff

cycle2.result: 20 of 27 areas (74%) met or exceeded the 10% change target; sensation screening +75%, rehabilitation +100%, neglect screening +92%, neglect assessment 100%.

audits.other_findings: Four audits in total. Anxiety and depression screening fell (-27%) and patient education about stroke barely changed (6%).
audits.citation: Vratsistas-Curto A, McCluskey A, Schurr K. Use of audit, feedback and education increased guideline implementation in a multidisciplinary stroke unit. BMJ Open Qual. 2017;6(2):e000212. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2017-000212. PMID: 29450304.

audits.title: Changing occupational therapy and physiotherapy practice through guidelines and audit in the United Kingdom.
audits.standard: National Clinical Guidelines for Stroke occupational therapy and physiotherapy recommendations
audits.setting: 235 hospitals in England, Wales and Northern Ireland (National Sentinel Audit of Stroke)

cycle1.result: Low rates of compliance with national standards across all domains.

audits.other_findings: Domains covered approaches to rehabilitation, carers and families, interventions and transfer to the community.

audits.title: Adherence to clinical guidelines improves patient outcomes in Australian audit of stroke rehabilitation practice.
audits.standard: Australian Clinical Guidelines for Stroke Rehabilitation and Recovery

cycle1.result: Evidence-based management delivered: treatment for sensorimotor impairment 38%, hypertonicity 56%, mobility 94%, home assessments 71%.

audits.other_findings: Units providing evidence-based management had better recovery outcomes; discharge FIM of 100 strongly correlated with discharge home.
audits.citation: Hubbard IJ, Harris D, Kilkenny MF, Faux SG, Pollack MR, Cadilhac DA. Adherence to clinical guidelines improves patient outcomes in Australian audit of stroke rehabilitation practice. Arch Phys Med Rehabil. 2012;93(6):965-971. doi:10.1016/j.apmr.2012.01.011. PMID: 22480546.

audits.title: Supporting clinical practice behavior change among neurologic physical therapists: a case study in knowledge translation.
audits.standard: Appropriate use of nonsupported gait training for eligible patients with hemiparesis
audits.setting: Inpatient rehabilitation stroke and brain injury physical therapy teams, UPMC Centers for Rehab Services, Pittsburgh

cycle1.result: 50% of eligible patients trained with nonsupported gait training.

audits.intervention: Quarterly staff meetings, group and individual dialogue, chart audit with aggregate feedback, reminders, role modelling and clinical consultation.

cycle2.result: 73% of eligible patients trained with nonsupported gait training.

audits.other_findings: 60% in the second quarter; therapists very or moderately familiar rose from 19% to 78% at 6 months.
audits.citation: Perry SB, Zeleznik H, Breisinger T. Supporting clinical practice behavior change among neurologic physical therapists: a case study in knowledge translation. J Neurol Phys Ther. 2014;38(2):134-143. doi:10.1097/npt.0000000000000034. PMID: 24637932.

audits.title: Criteria audit as a means of assessing the physiotherapy component of stroke rehabilitation.
audits.setting: Rehabilitation wards, Bendigo Home and Hospital for the Aged

cycle1.result: Problem areas in documentation, outcome, complications and integrated care.

audits.intervention: Physiotherapy measures to improve outcome and integrated care and reduce complications.
audits.other_findings: A third audit was in progress.
